grades.reason: Describes xv6 user-trap entry: uservec switches satp to the kernel page table and jumps to usertrap. It also explains how userret switches satp back and why the trampoline mapping lets execution continue. It never mentions SFENCE.VMA or TLB synchronization, so it answers only the satp half.

grades.quote: The CPU doesn’t switch to the kernel page table, doesn’t switch to a stack in the kernel, and doesn’t save any registers other than the pc. Kernel software must perform these tasks.
grades.reason: Gives background on RISC-V trap hardware and says the CPU does not switch page tables on a trap, so software must. It does not describe what writing satp does in uservec or why SFENCE.VMA is used.

grades.quote: The instruction orders stores only to HS-level address-translation structures with subsequent HS-level address translations.
grades.reason: Describes SFENCE.VMA semantics in the RISC-V H-extension, where it orders stores to address-translation structures against later translations. This is generic background on the instruction. It has nothing to do with xv6 trap entry or satp switching.

grades.quote: To tell a CPU to use a page table, the kernel must write the physical address of the root pagetable page into the satp register. A CPU will translate all addresses generated by subsequent instructions using the page table pointed to by its satp.
grades.reason: Gives a general xv6 explanation of what writing satp does: the CPU uses the page table it points to for all later address translation. It is not specific to trap entry and does not cover SFENCE.VMA or TLB flushing.
